value.rationale: Twelve icosahedral vertex-tangent measurements are a canonical fixed-degree spherical Hermite interpolation problem. The degree-eight and fourteen resurgence of a three-dimensional loss after earlier surjectivity is a nonmonotonic structural phenomenon; the degree-fourteen final obstruction and universal degree-fifteen threshold exactly characterize the sampling capability. This is not a parameter-renaming or an isolated arbitrary numerical determinant: it is an all-degree theorem with a substantial analytic tail and an independently meaningful derivative-observation target. Similar scalar value sampling patterns are credited without treating them as the same invariant.
